paragraphs.text: THE 71-DAY PASSAGE
THE ANDEAN CARAVAN
THE GUIDE IN YOUR HAND
A proposal you can picture yourself inside
A caravan is not a race down a route. It is a moving circle travellers, hosts, vehicles and local knowledge progressing slowly enough for each place to change the terms.

This guide shows the intended experience of the Andean Caravan in clear, day-by-day form. You may travel one section, combine consecutive sections, take the eight-day Stone Road, or follow the whole 71-day passage from Lima to Balmaceda.
IMPORTANT
This is a route proposal, not yet a confirmed departure.

It communicates the intended route, pace and level of effort. Exact dates, named properties, suppliers, tickets, departure times, prices and meal inclusions become final only after the 2028 operating plan is secured. Weather, permits, border authorities and vessel operators can change the order or content of a day; the guide names those dependencies wherever they affect your choice.
THE WHOLE PASSAGE
From the Pacific to the end of the road

Four sections tile one continuous journey. The gates are where the group may change; between them, the Caravan remains together. Cusco is the single additional joining point, and only for The Stone Road.
23 days	16 days	18 days	14 days
LIMA	PUNO	SUCRE	SANTIAGO	BALMACEDA
CUSCO JOINS THE 8-DAY STONE ROAD ONLY
04	The End of the Road	Santiago - Balmaceda	14 days
HOW THE CARAVAN WORKS
Fixed gates, shared rhythm
Five Caravan gates

Lima, Puno, Sucre, Santiago and Balmaceda are the only Caravan gates. Join and leave only at the gate attached to the section you choose. There is no roadside boarding and no other mid-section joining.
One short-form joining point

The Stone Road joins the existing Caravan at Cusco for Days 16-23 and ends at Puno. Travellers arrive in Cusco by the previous evening; Day 16 is deliberately protected for orientation and recovery. The short form shares Section 01's maximum of 12 places.
A changing group, with continuity

Some travellers may leave as others join at a gate. A through-journey steward carries continuity across all four sections, while a section host brings local and operational responsibility to each passage. Gate days protect arrivals, departures and the group's reset.
Fixed dates. Five Caravan gates. Advance booking. Maximum 12.
MOVEMENT
Overland wherever the route can remain continuous
Most of the journey travels by road, rail, passenger boat, vehicle ferry or 4x4 convoy. Peru and Bolivia meet at the Kasani foot border; Bolivia and Chile meet at Hito Cajon with a vehicle change.

Scheduled	Five movements are planned within the product: Arequipa-Cusco, LaPaz-Sucre, Calama-Santiago, Santiago-Balmaceda and the Day 71 flights	Balmaceda-Santiago exit. All depend on secured 2028 timetables.
Road	Some days are long and some surfaces are rough. Comfort stops, driverhours, luggage capacity and no planned night driving form part of the
operating standard.
READING EACH DAY
Effort is more than walking distance
Every day separates physical effort from the operating environment. A short day can still be demanding if it sleeps high, begins early, changes hotels or removes access to easy recovery.
FREE TIME
When the guide says free time, it means genuinely uncommitted time. It is not a space waiting to be filled later by a compulsory tour.
BEFORE YOU CHOOSE
The honest shape of the journey
Altitude

The route reaches approximately 4,900-4,980 m and includes three expected refuge nights around 4,100-4,600 m. Individual medical advice is part of choosing well; an itinerary can design progression but cannot guarantee how a body responds.
Access

Tortel is not step-free. Taquile, Isla del Sol, Machu Picchu and several archaeological sites involve steps, stone, uneven ground, exposed surfaces or small-vessel boarding. Adapted routes reduce barriers; they do not erase them.
Remote conditions
The Lagunas crossing uses simple refuges with shared bathrooms and limited heating. Parts of Patagonia have limited services, ripio road, ferry dependencies and weather-controlled vessel days.
Luggage
Several transitions use a soft overnight bag while main luggage travels separately. Final weight limits, carrying distances, porterage and stair routes will be published before deposits.
Conditions have authority

The Caravan does not promise wildlife, clear skies, calm water, a salt mirror or an unobstructed monument. Where access depends on weather, permits or an operator, the itinerary protects a second window, a buffer or a meaningful fallback.

SECTION 01 · DAYS 1-23 SEA TO STONE
Pacific coast, desert, deep canyon and the Stone Road
GATE TO GATE
Lima to Puno
23 days · Maximum 12 travellers
THE ANDEAN CARAVAN
SECTION 01 · AT A GLANCE
Sea to Stone

From sea level, the Caravan moves slowly south through Peru's coastal desert, climbs to Arequipa and Colca, then reaches Cusco, the Sacred Valley and two separately ticketed visits to Machu Picchu before crossing the altiplano to Puno.
THE STAGES
Desert Coast	Days 1-8
White City, Deep Canyon	Days 9-15
The Stone Road	Days 16-23 - also available as the short form
THE STONE ROAD · 8 DAYS
Days 16-23 may be booked as the short form from Cusco to Puno. Join by the previous evening; Day 16 is protected. The Stone Road joins the existing group and shares the same 12-place capacity.
SECTION 01 · BEFORE YOU CHOOSE
Where this section asks more of you
·  Day 4 and Day 8 are long road days; Days 6 and 7 are multi-stop days with hotel changes.
·  Pachacámac, Tambo Colorado, Chauchilla and Sacaco are exposed to heat and sun, with uneven or unsealed ground.
·  Patapampa at 4,910 m is the second-highest point on the whole Caravan and is reached on Day
·  Cruz del Cóndor involves an early start, cold, standing and uneven viewing areas.
·  Pisac, Ollantaytambo and both Machu Picchu entries use stone, steps and wet-season surfaces. Machu Picchu requires timed, one-way circuits; a person cannot leave and re-enter on the same ticket.
·  Day 23 is more than ten hours on the train and crosses approximately 4,335 m at La Raya.

·  The section ends at 3,800 m. A traveller leaving at Puno should plan their onward travel with that in mind. FOR SHORT-FORM TRAVELLERS The eight days begin at 3,400 m and end at 3,800 m, with a descent into the Sacred Valley in between. The demanding days are 20, 21 and 23. Individual medical advice about altitude is required in the same terms as for the full section.
SLEEP PATTERN

Lima three nights, Paracas two, Nazca one, Chala one, Arequipa three across two stops, one Colca base for three nights, Cusco four nights across two stops, one night near Urubamba, one at Ollantaytambo, one at Machu Picchu Pueblo, and the Puno gate night. Chala and Machu Picchu Pueblo are the two properties requiring the closest inspection.
SAWA··YATRA
SECTION 02 · DAYS 24-39 BOTH SHORES
Titicaca, La Paz and the cloud forest
GATE TO GATE
Puno to Sucre
16 days · Maximum 12 travellers
THE ANDEAN CARAVAN
SECTION 02 · AT A GLANCE
Both Shores
A lake-and-city journey at altitude: the inhabited islands of Titicaca, a foot crossing into Bolivia, Isla del Sol, La Paz and Tiwanaku, then a descent into the Yungas before flying to Sucre.
THE STAGES
The Islands and theBorder	Days 24-31
Thin Air and Cloud Forest	Days 32-39
SECTION 02 · BEFORE YOU CHOOSE
Where this section asks more of you
·  Most of the section is spent above 3,600 m, apart from the two Coroico nights at approximately 1,700 m and the final Sucre gate night at approximately 2,800 m.
·  Three days use small passenger boats at high altitude. Boarding, toilet, shade, warmth and motion exposure require exact disclosure.
·  Taquile and Isla del Sol contain steep paths and substantial steps. Planned landings and shorter routes reduce the barrier but do not create step-free access.
·  The optional Pachatata route rises above 4,100 m before breakfast. A lower route is offered without penalty.
·  Kasani is an international border. Queues, document issues and the cross-border vehicle change can extend the day.
·  The Coroico road is subject to wet-season landslides and closures. The modern road is used, never the Death Road.
·  The section ends with a scheduled flight that the structure depends on. The road alternative is not a same-day substitute.
SLEEP PATTERN
Puno four nights across the stage, including the Day 27 buffer. Copacabana two, Amantaní one family house, Isla del Sol one. La Paz five nights across two stops, with Day 35 held entirely open.
Coroico two. Sucre closes the section at the Caravan standard and is the gate night for Section 03.
SAWA··YATRA
SECTION 03 · DAYS 40-57 THE MIRROR
Silver cities, wet-season salt, high lagoons and the Atacama
GATE TO GATE
Sucre to Santiago
18 days · Maximum 12 travellers
THE ANDEAN CARAVAN
SECTION 03 · AT A GLANCE
The Mirror

The Caravan begins gently in Sucre, climbs through Potosi and Uyuni, then commits to its most remote passage: the Salar, the Lagunas, three refuge nights and the high border into Chile before recovering in the Atacama and flying to Santiago.
THE STAGES
Silver and Bone	Days 40-46
The Salar and the Lagunas	Days 47-53
Red Earth, Open Sky	Days 54-57
SECTION 03 · BEFORE YOU CHOOSE
Where this section asks more of you
·  Five consecutive Demanding days under a Declared Load Exception, with three refuge nights at approximately 4,100 to 4,600 m, shared bathrooms and limited heating.
·  The route reaches approximately 4,900 m and may approach 4,980 m at Sol de Mañana.
·  Potosí is reached at 4,090 m after a sleeping-altitude gain of more than 1,200 m from Sucre.
·  Rough track, cold, wind and repeated vehicle entry require a specific mobility and seating assessment.
·  Day 53 combines a pre-dawn start, the highest point, border formalities and a long descent.
·  The section is a long way from a hospital for four of its days.
·  Maragua uses a road that can be affected by rain; an equally considered Sucre alternative is required.
SLEEP PATTERN

Sucre three nights, Potosí two, Uyuni two. Two nights on the Salar's north shore, one at San Juan or Colcha K, three refuges. San Pedro de Atacama four consecutive nights with no repacking, from the Day 53 arrival through Day 56. The Santiago gate night closes the section.
A clear threshold

This is the expedition section. A traveller who wants Titicaca, La Paz and Sucre without the Salar crossing can end at Sucre. A traveller joining The Mirror chooses the altitude, refuge conditions and consecutive load described here.
SAWA··YATRA
SECTION 04 · DAYS 58-71
THE END OF THE ROAD
The Carretera Austral to Villa O'Higgins and back to the ferry
GATE TO GATE
Santiago to Balmaceda
14 days · Maximum 12 travellers
THE ANDEAN CARAVAN
SECTION 04 · AT A GLANCE
The End of the Road

A Patagonian road-and-water passage through Aysen: Cerro Castillo, the Marble Chapels, Cochrane, Tortel and Villa O'Higgins, followed by the necessary return north to the Chile Chico ferry and a closing day in Coyhaique.
THE STAGES
Aysen and the Lake	Days 58-61
Tortel and the Fjord	Days 62-65
The Return and the Ferry	Days 66-71
SECTION 04 · BEFORE YOU CHOOSE
Where this section asks more of you
·  Ripio, long seated days, three vehicle-ferry crossings on two services and two planned, weather-dependent small-vessel experiences.
·  Tortel is reached through boardwalks and stairs and is not step-free.
·  The O'Higgins Glacier sailing and Marble Chapels navigation are weather-dependent and may not operate at all.
·  Day 66 is followed by two Steady road days before the ferry-heavy Day 69. There is no three-day demanding return cluster.
·  April accommodation and services are thinner than high summer. Every property must confirm it remains open for the exact dates.
SLEEP PATTERN

Coyhaique three nights across two stops. Río Tranquilo and Villa O'Higgins each hold two or more nights to create weather windows. Cochrane is used in both directions. Puerto Guadal is an overnight. Coyhaique holds the final two nights as the ferry, closure and flight buffer.
Why the road returns

Villa O'Higgins is the geographic end of the southbound road. The product then retraces north through Cochrane and Puerto Guadal to reach the Chile Chico ferry and Balmaceda. The return is part of the route, not hidden backtracking.
WHAT HAPPENS NEXT
From route proposal to your departure

This guide is the clearest picture of the intended journey. Before any section is offered as a secured departure, Sawayatra will reconcile the calendar, contract the route-critical trains, flights, ferries, refuges and local encounters, inspect access and accommodation, and publish the exact inclusion and cancellation terms.
03	Receive the	Dates, price, properties, flights, inclusions, medical andinsurance requirements, and the final day plan.
secured detail
The road is fixed.
The journey remains alive to weather, water and the people who hold each place.

Rail
Tourist rail serves Machu Picchu. A full-day premium train crosses Cusco to Puno; its operating day helps determine the entire Caravan calendar.
Water
Titicaca and Patagonia include small passenger vessels, lake navigation and vehicle ferries. Harbour, wind, water and operator decisions have authority over the day.
LIGHT
Arrival, recovery, buffer or compact programme. The point is to create room around the harder days.
STEADY
A normal travelling day: walking, road movement, a visit or a hotel change without concentrated load.
DEMANDING
Long movement, significant altitude, rough ground, early start, complex boarding or several load signals together.
CONNECTED
Reliable services and straightforward access to support.
LIMITED SERVICES
Fewer choices and slower access to support; planning matters.
REMOTE
Simple infrastructure, long transfer routes and limited communications or facilities.

HIGHEST POINT
4,910 m at Patapampa

SLEEP AT CLOSE
Approx. 3,800 m at Puno

MOVEMENT
Road, passenger boat, rail and one scheduled flight

SEASON
February - coastal summer and Andean wet season

DAY 01	Arrive in Lima

	ROUTE	SLEEP
	Lima	Lima

	MOVEMENT	RHYTHM
	Protected airport transfer	Light · Connected
A Host or named representative meets each arrival and brings the traveller to the first hotel. There is no group visit, welcome performance or concealed first-day schedule. The job of the day is to arrive.
Free time. The day remains uncommitted after check-in. A simple arrival meal may be offered once meal inclusions are set.

DAY 02	Objects before chronology

	ROUTE	SLEEP
	Lima	Lima

	MOVEMENT	RHYTHM
	City vehicle and short walks	Light · Connected
A guided morning at Museo Larco begins with material culture rather than a compressed history lecture. Lunch is unhurried. The afternoon is kept open for rest, a garden or an optional neighbourhood walk.
Free time. From mid-afternoon. A real free period, not an optional paid excursion inserted later.

DAY 03	Market, kitchens and Barranco

	ROUTE	SLEEP
	Lima	Lima

	MOVEMENT	RHYTHM
	Several short city transfers	Steady · Connected
The food day begins at Surquillo market, then follows a small number of ingredients through makers, kitchens or tables. Barranco belongs later in the day, when the light and the pace have both softened.
Free time. A quiet break is built between the food programme and Barranco. The evening is free.

DAY 04	Pachacámac and south to Paracas

	ROUTE	SLEEP
	Lima to Pachacámac to Paracas	Paracas

	MOVEMENT	RHYTHM
	Approx. 4.5 to 5.5 hours road plus site	Demanding · Limited services
The Caravan leaves Lima early on the Panamericana Sur and stops at Pachacámac within the first hour, where the site sits on the road rather than at the end of a return excursion. The site is exposed, uneven and larger than the group needs to cover on foot; vehicle-supported interpretation keeps the visit complete without treating distance as achievement. The road then continues to Paracas, and the evening is left alone.
Free time. After arrival and check-in. No sunset activity is fixed to a traffic-sensitive day.

DAY 05	Ballestas and the red coast

	ROUTE	SLEEP
	Paracas	Paracas

	MOVEMENT	RHYTHM
	Boat block and reserve road	Steady · Limited services
An early passenger boat goes towards the Ballestas Islands only when the harbour authority clears departures. The reserve follows by road, with the red coast and desert doing the work that the boat cannot be asked to guarantee.
Free time. Late afternoon and evening at the same base.

Tambo Colorado, Huacachina and the road to
DAY 06 Nazca

	ROUTE	SLEEP
	Paracas to Tambo Colorado to Huacachina to Nazca	Nazca

	MOVEMENT	RHYTHM
	Approx. 5 hours road across the day	Steady · Limited services
The day turns inland for a contained visit to Tambo Colorado, then returns to the valley road. The route pauses at Huacachina without turning the oasis into a compulsory dune-buggy day. After a quiet lunch the Caravan continues to Nazca.
Free time. A contained pause at Huacachina and a free evening in Nazca.

DAY 07	The lines from the ground, Chauchilla and Sacaco

	ROUTE	SLEEP
	Nazca to Chauchilla to Sacaco to Chala	Chala

	MOVEMENT	RHYTHM
	Approx. 4 to 5 hours road plus sites	Steady · Limited services
The morning reads the Nazca lines from the mirador and the interpretive record - how they were made, who made them, what the desert surface does and does not preserve. Chauchilla follows, with its exposed cemetery landscape. After lunch the road turns south through Sacaco and its fossil marine beds to Chala on the coast.
Free time. A quiet evening in Chala after a multi-stop day.

DAY 08	The climb to Arequipa

	ROUTE	SLEEP
	Chala to Arequipa	Arequipa

	MOVEMENT	RHYTHM
	Approx. 7 to 8 hours road	Demanding · Limited services
One steady road day completes the coast. Meal and comfort stops are part of the plan. The road climbs from the Pacific to 2,335 m, and Arequipa is an arrival rather than one more visit.
Free time. Only after check-in. The evening has no scheduled group content.

DAY 09	Arequipa, first acclimatisation day

	ROUTE	SLEEP
	Arequipa	Arequipa

	MOVEMENT	RHYTHM
	Short local movement	Light · Connected
A brief Host-led orientation is the only fixed content. The city is read from a compact route, with the afternoon returned to the traveller.
Free time. Most of the afternoon and evening.

DAY 10	Arequipa, second acclimatisation day

	ROUTE	SLEEP
	Arequipa	Arequipa

	MOVEMENT	RHYTHM
	Half-day city visit	Light · Connected
One cultural visit occupies the morning. The remainder stays deliberately unprogrammed before the following day's high pass. Distance on foot is adjusted through vehicle support and a shorter interior route.
Free time. From lunch onwards.

DAY 11	Across Patapampa into Colca

	ROUTE	SLEEP
	Arequipa to Patapampa to Colca	Yanque or Chivay

	MOVEMENT	RHYTHM
	Approx. 4.5 to 5.5 hours road	Demanding · Limited services
The road crosses the high plateau and pauses only briefly at Patapampa. There is no walk staged at 4,910 m. The vehicle then descends to the chosen valley base, where the evening remains quiet.
Free time. After check-in. No added village circuit is attached to the arrival day.

DAY 12	Terraces and valley communities

	ROUTE	SLEEP
	Colca Valley	Same Colca base

	MOVEMENT	RHYTHM
	Short road links and uneven walks	Steady · Limited services
A contained morning follows selected terraces and communities rather than collecting every viewpoint. Local participation will be agreed and credited. The group returns to the same hotel before lunch or in the early afternoon.
Free time. A substantial afternoon at the same base.

DAY 13	Condor country, without a promise

	ROUTE	SLEEP
	Colca Valley and Cruz del Cóndor	Same Colca base

	MOVEMENT	RHYTHM
	Early road outing	Steady · Limited services
The group leaves early for Cruz del Cóndor, then returns through a small number of valley stops.
Condors may use the morning thermals. Their appearance is not an inclusion. Cold, standing and rain are disclosed as part of the visit.
Free time. The afternoon remains open at the same property.

DAY 14	Return to Arequipa

	ROUTE	SLEEP
	Colca to Arequipa	Arequipa

	MOVEMENT	RHYTHM
	Approx. 4 to 5 hours road	Steady · Limited services
The Caravan returns to Arequipa without adding a second major visit. The afternoon and evening absorb road conditions, laundry and the practical work of the following flight.
Free time. After arrival.

DAY 15	Fly to Cusco

	ROUTE	SLEEP
	Arequipa to Cusco	Cusco

	MOVEMENT	RHYTHM
	Scheduled flight; approx. 4 to 5 hours door to door	Light · Connected
A direct scheduled flight is used if the secured 2028 timetable supports it. Nothing is programmed after arrival.
Free time. After check-in.

DAY 16	Cusco, arrival pace

	ROUTE	SLEEP
	Cusco	Cusco

	MOVEMENT	RHYTHM
	Short orientation	Light · Connected
A compact orientation, and the rest of the day open. No arrival activity is required at 3,400 m.
Free time. Most of the day.

DAY 17	Cusco at a slower pace

	ROUTE	SLEEP
	Cusco	Cusco

	MOVEMENT	RHYTHM
	City vehicle and adapted walk	Light · Connected
One compact morning visit gives the city room without stacking a monument circuit. Cobbles and steps are shortened by vehicle placement. Lunch is followed by an uncommitted afternoon.
Free time. From early afternoon.

DAY 18	Pisac and the Sacred Valley

	ROUTE	SLEEP
	Cusco to Pisac to Urubamba	Urubamba area

	MOVEMENT	RHYTHM
	Approx. 2 to 3 hours road across the day	Steady · Limited services
The group uses the upper vehicle access for a shortened archaeological route at Pisac, then descends into the Sacred Valley. The day ends near Urubamba rather than returning uphill to Cusco.
Free time. Late afternoon at the valley base.

DAY 19	Maras, Moray and Ollantaytambo

	ROUTE	SLEEP
	Urubamba to Maras and Moray to Ollantaytambo	Ollantaytambo

	MOVEMENT	RHYTHM
	Approx. 2 to 3 hours road	Steady · Limited services
Moray is visited in the morning, followed by Ollantaytambo town and an adapted archaeological route. The upper temple climb remains optional. Lower precincts and the town are treated as a complete visit, not a consolation.
Free time. A quiet evening in Ollantaytambo before the train movement.

DAY 20	First Machu Picchu entry

	ROUTE	SLEEP
	Ollantaytambo to Machu Picchu Pueblo	Machu Picchu Pueblo

	MOVEMENT	RHYTHM
	Rail, bus and timed walking circuit	Demanding · Limited services
A morning train reaches Machu Picchu Pueblo. After the overnight bag is left at the hotel, the group takes the bus to a separately ticketed afternoon entry, planned around a panoramic route under the rules then in force.
Free time. A short pause between hotel arrival and the timed entry. The evening is free after return to town.

DAY 21	Second entry and return to Cusco

	ROUTE	SLEEP
	Machu Picchu Pueblo to Cusco	Cusco

	MOVEMENT	RHYTHM
	Bus, walking circuit, rail and road	Demanding · Limited services
A second, separately ticketed morning entry is planned around a complementary lower route. After lunch the group returns by rail and road to Cusco. This is the stage's highest walking effort and one of its longer movement days.
Free time. Only after arrival in Cusco.

DAY 22	Cusco weather buffer

	ROUTE	SLEEP
	Cusco	Cusco

	MOVEMENT	RHYTHM
	None unless recovery is required	Light · Connected
The entire day is held open. If rail or permit movement has slipped, it protects the stage. If the route has run to schedule, the day belongs to rest, laundry and individual time. It is not back-filled with a compulsory tour.
Free time. The whole day when the buffer is not needed.

DAY 23	Across the altiplano by day train, and the Puno gate

	ROUTE	SLEEP
	Cusco to Puno	Puno

	MOVEMENT	RHYTHM
	Current service approx. 10 hours 30 minutes	Demanding · Limited services
The PeruRail Titicaca day train crosses the altiplano and La Raya before arriving in Puno in the early evening. Dining, live music and traditional dance are part of the present service model. The day is low in walking and long in sitting.
For travellers ending here, this is the last day of the Caravan. For travellers continuing, the Puno night is the gate: the close of Section 01 and the protected beginning of Section 02.
Free time. None is promised beyond the train journey and arrival evening.

HIGHEST POINT
Approx. 4,115 m at Pachatata

SLEEP RANGE
Approx. 1,700 m to 3,850 m

MOVEMENT
Road, passenger boat, vehicle barge, foot border and flight

SEASON
Late February to mid-March - wet season

DAY 24	Uros, then a quiet Puno afternoon

	ROUTE	SLEEP
	Puno to Uros to Puno	Puno

	MOVEMENT	RHYTHM
	Half-day passenger boat	Light · Limited services
A contained morning reaches Uros and returns to Puno. The visit is community-led and avoids treating the islands as floating scenery. The afternoon is protected after the previous day's long train, or after the joiner's arrival progression.
Free time. From early afternoon.

DAY 25	Taquile to Amantaní

	ROUTE	SLEEP
	Puno to Taquile to Amantaní	Family house on Amantaní

	MOVEMENT	RHYTHM
	Approx. 4 to 5 hours boat across the day	Demanding · Remote
An early proposed private launch reaches Taquile through a community-agreed landing with a smaller climb. This reduces, but does not remove, steps. A shortened textile and cultural visit with lunch is followed by the inter-island boat to Amantaní, aiming to arrive by mid-afternoon and well before dark.
Free time. A quiet period after meeting the host family and settling in.

DAY 26	Amantaní with two morning routes

	ROUTE	SLEEP
	Amantaní to Puno	Puno

	MOVEMENT	RHYTHM
	Optional hill walk and approx. 3.5 hours boat	Steady · Remote
An early visit towards Pachatata is offered only with the host community and when local access permits. It is optional. A village-level morning is a complete parallel choice. The boat returns to Puno in early afternoon.
Free time. After the return to Puno.

DAY 27	Puno, and the day the lake may have taken

ROUTE	SLEEP Puno	Puno

	MOVEMENT	RHYTHM
	None unless recovery or recovery of lost island time is required	Light · Connected
The whole day is held. If wind or swell shortened Taquile, displaced the Amantaní stay or forced an early return, this is where that time is recovered - with the community, at the community's convenience, not squeezed into an already-full day. If the lake behaved, the day belongs to rest, laundry, a slower Puno and individual time before the border.
Free time. The whole day when the buffer is not needed.

DAY 28	Walk the border at Kasani

	ROUTE	SLEEP
	Puno to Kasani to Copacabana	Copacabana

	MOVEMENT	RHYTHM
	Approx. 4 to 6 hours road and formalities	Steady · Limited services
The road reaches Kasani, where travellers complete Peruvian and Bolivian controls and walk the short distance between them. Vehicles and luggage transfer under the arranged cross-border plan.
Copacabana is the day's end, not a launch point for another boat.
Free time. After border completion and check-in.

DAY 29	Cross to Isla del Sol

	ROUTE	SLEEP
	Copacabana to Isla del Sol	Southern Isla del Sol

	MOVEMENT	RHYTHM
	Approx. 1.5 to 2 hours boat	Steady · Remote
A passenger boat reaches the southern or Yumani sector. The day uses a short island route rather than a full ridge traverse. Luggage assistance is arranged from the landing to the selected property.
Free time. A substantial late afternoon on the island.

DAY 30	Isla del Sol, then Copacabana

	ROUTE	SLEEP
	Isla del Sol to Copacabana	Copacabana

	MOVEMENT	RHYTHM
	Short walk and passenger boat	Steady · Remote
A short southern-island route uses paths confirmed locally open at the time. The group returns to Copacabana in early afternoon. The schedule does not depend on crossing the entire island.
Free time. The afternoon in Copacabana.

DAY 31	Tiquina and the descent into La Paz

	ROUTE	SLEEP
	Copacabana to Tiquina to La Paz	La Paz

	MOVEMENT	RHYTHM
	Approx. 4 to 5.5 hours road and barge	Steady · Limited services
The vehicle crosses the Tiquina strait by barge before the road rises to El Alto and descends into La Paz. Nothing is programmed after check-in.
Free time. After arrival.

DAY 32	La Paz from above

	ROUTE	SLEEP
	La Paz	La Paz

	MOVEMENT	RHYTHM
	Cable car and short road links	Light · Connected

THE ANDEAN CARAVAN
THE GUIDE IN YOUR HAND
A proposal you can picture yourself inside
A caravan is not a race down a route. It is a moving circle travellers, hosts, vehicles and local knowledge progressing slowly enough for each place to change the terms.

HOW THE CARAVAN WORKS
Fixed gates, shared rhythm
Five Caravan gates

Lima, Puno, Sucre, Santiago and Balmaceda are the only Caravan gates. Join and leave only at the gate attached to the section you choose. There is no roadside boarding and no other mid-section joining.
One short-form joining point

The Stone Road joins the existing Caravan at Cusco for Days 16-23 and ends at Puno. Travellers arrive in Cusco by the previous evening; Day 16 is deliberately protected for orientation and recovery. The short form shares Section 01's maximum of 12 places.
A changing group, with continuity

Some travellers may leave as others join at a gate. A through-journey steward carries continuity across all four sections, while a section host brings local and operational responsibility to each passage. Gate days protect arrivals, departures and the group's reset.
Fixed dates. Five Caravan gates. Advance booking. Maximum 12.
MOVEMENT
Overland wherever the route can remain continuous
Most of the journey travels by road, rail, passenger boat, vehicle ferry or 4x4 convoy. Peru and Bolivia meet at the Kasani foot border; Bolivia and Chile meet at Hito Cajon with a vehicle change.

record.text: FREE TIME
When the guide says free time, it means genuinely uncommitted time. It is not a space waiting to be filled later by a compulsory tour.
BEFORE YOU CHOOSE
The honest shape of the journey
Altitude

The route reaches approximately 4,900-4,980 m and includes three expected refuge nights around 4,100-4,600 m. Individual medical advice is part of choosing well; an itinerary can design progression but cannot guarantee how a body responds.
Access

Tortel is not step-free. Taquile, Isla del Sol, Machu Picchu and several archaeological sites involve steps, stone, uneven ground, exposed surfaces or small-vessel boarding. Adapted routes reduce barriers; they do not erase them.
Remote conditions
The Lagunas crossing uses simple refuges with shared bathrooms and limited heating. Parts of Patagonia have limited services, ripio road, ferry dependencies and weather-controlled vessel days.
Luggage
Several transitions use a soft overnight bag while main luggage travels separately. Final weight limits, carrying distances, porterage and stair routes will be published before deposits.
Conditions have authority

The Caravan does not promise wildlife, clear skies, calm water, a salt mirror or an unobstructed monument. Where access depends on weather, permits or an operator, the itinerary protects a second window, a buffer or a meaningful fallback.

Where this section asks more of you
·  Day 4 and Day 8 are long road days; Days 6 and 7 are multi-stop days with hotel changes.

record.text: SECTION 02 · BEFORE YOU CHOOSE
Where this section asks more of you
·  Most of the section is spent above 3,600 m, apart from the two Coroico nights at approximately 1,700 m and the final Sucre gate night at approximately 2,800 m.
·  Three days use small passenger boats at high altitude. Boarding, toilet, shade, warmth and motion exposure require exact disclosure.
·  Taquile and Isla del Sol contain steep paths and substantial steps. Planned landings and shorter routes reduce the barrier but do not create step-free access.
·  The optional Pachatata route rises above 4,100 m before breakfast. A lower route is offered without penalty.
·  Kasani is an international border. Queues, document issues and the cross-border vehicle change can extend the day.
·  The Coroico road is subject to wet-season landslides and closures. The modern road is used, never the Death Road.
·  The section ends with a scheduled flight that the structure depends on. The road alternative is not a same-day substitute.
SLEEP PATTERN
Puno four nights across the stage, including the Day 27 buffer. Copacabana two, Amantaní one family house, Isla del Sol one. La Paz five nights across two stops, with Day 35 held entirely open.
Coroico two. Sucre closes the section at the Caravan standard and is the gate night for Section 03.

·  Potosí is reached at 4,090 m after a sleeping-altitude gain of more than 1,200 m from Sucre.
·  Rough track, cold, wind and repeated vehicle entry require a specific mobility and seating assessment.
·  Day 53 combines a pre-dawn start, the highest point, border formalities and a long descent.
·  The section is a long way from a hospital for four of its days.
·  Maragua uses a road that can be affected by rain; an equally considered Sucre alternative is required.
SLEEP PATTERN

Sucre three nights, Potosí two, Uyuni two. Two nights on the Salar's north shore, one at San Juan or Colcha K, three refuges. San Pedro de Atacama four consecutive nights with no repacking, from the Day 53 arrival through Day 56. The Santiago gate night closes the section.
A clear threshold

This is the expedition section. A traveller who wants Titicaca, La Paz and Sucre without the Salar crossing can end at Sucre. A traveller joining The Mirror chooses the altitude, refuge conditions and consecutive load described here.

record.text: SECTION 04 · BEFORE YOU CHOOSE
Where this section asks more of you
·  Ripio, long seated days, three vehicle-ferry crossings on two services and two planned, weather-dependent small-vessel experiences.
·  Tortel is reached through boardwalks and stairs and is not step-free.
·  The O'Higgins Glacier sailing and Marble Chapels navigation are weather-dependent and may not operate at all.
·  Day 66 is followed by two Steady road days before the ferry-heavy Day 69. There is no three-day demanding return cluster.
·  April accommodation and services are thinner than high summer. Every property must confirm it remains open for the exact dates.
SLEEP PATTERN

Coyhaique three nights across two stops. Río Tranquilo and Villa O'Higgins each hold two or more nights to create weather windows. Cochrane is used in both directions. Puerto Guadal is an overnight. Coyhaique holds the final two nights as the ferry, closure and flight buffer.
Why the road returns

Villa O'Higgins is the geographic end of the southbound road. The product then retraces north through Cochrane and Puerto Guadal to reach the Chile Chico ferry and Balmaceda. The return is part of the route, not hidden backtracking.
